investor_capital_decision: Steelmaker/trading-house JV builds EAF and thin-slab casting beside Rudny's proposed iron-reduction chain.
buyer_market: Prospective Turkish/EU re-rollers; qualified slab demand and transport route UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: September 2026 reporting says ERG deferred HBI indefinitely [S02]; original downstream trigger has weakened.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Incumbent slab supply to Turkey/EU; coastal integrated DRI/EAF candidates. Strongest slab-specific supplier not established.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: firm hot-DRI access plus reliable power and delivered slab cost.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: adjacency cannot monetize hot charging until upstream plant, transfer arrangement and EAF utilities are committed.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: no slab tonnage/offtake. Original HBI nameplate is neither current firm capacity nor slab demand.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: EAF grid capacity, gas, water, hot-DRI configuration and export freight.
captured_status: FACT: old HBI contract [S01]; later deferral/lapsed-contract report [S02]. No open downstream equity/site agreement established.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: avoided iron cooling/reheating and integrated conversion margin, conditional on actual hot feed.
cheapest_kill_test: Is the proposed upstream hot-iron chain still executable on a sponsor-backed timetable?
decisive_evidence: FACT: ERG's 2025 scope is HBI [S01]. Kazinform attributes indefinite deferral and unfinalized financing to ERG [S02].
key_unknown: Whether sponsor will restart and offer downstream hot feed, site rights and utilities.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK for timing/dependency. A new capital-intensive downstream plant rests on an upstream project now deferred; this is not proof permanent infeasibility.

investor_capital_decision: OEM-qualified wheel maker builds low-pressure casting, machining and finishing capacity in proposed Kostanay location.
buyer_market: Kazakh assemblers, then eligible EAEU/Uzbek customers; model-level nominations UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: automotive output/localization drive exists [S03]; named Astana Motors wheel JV is at MoU stage [S04].
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing qualified imported wheels and planned Astana Motors/Hands JV; Russian K&K is a technical rival precedent [S05].
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: qualified recurring model volume and delivered cost, including tooling and metal freight.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local replenishment can help; Kostanay lacks an established liquid-metal link. K&K discloses one [S05].
scale_view: CALCULATION: 2026 plan of 177k passenger cars [S03] x 4 fitted wheels (ASSUMPTION) = 708k wheels before alloy share/captive supply; plan, not sales.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: alloy specification, melt/remelt cost, OEM testing and site power.
captured_status: FACT: named three-party MoU prioritizes Astana Motors' own plants [S04]; no proof all other OEM demand or all equity is closed.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: nominated OEM orders amortize tooling and reduce inbound component freight/inventory.
cheapest_kill_test: Have existing nominations and the announced JV already absorbed economically viable wheel volume?
decisive_evidence: FACT: MoU names Astana Motors, Open Element and Hands [S04]. Government reports 171k vehicles produced in 2025 [S03].
key_unknown: Does a distinct unawarded alloy-wheel programme remain large enough for a Kostanay line?
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 45-min desk/RFQ brief: obtain Allur/Kia model wheel BOMs, annual volumes and nomination status; compare rival quotes with line supplier breakeven volume.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Unawarded compatible models cover quoted breakeven throughput; OEM accepts qualification route and local landed cost matches qualified imports.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if only fragmented residual models remain; FAIL only if binding nominations exclude the target programme or measured cost cannot compete.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. Real localization interest supports the mechanism, but named partners and a small fragmented volume base make the remaining slot decisive. MoU alone is not capture.

investor_capital_decision: Qualified automotive caster builds high-pressure structural die-casting capacity in the proposed Kostanay cluster.
buyer_market: Specific regional vehicle platforms buying structural castings; component families UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: government instructed creation of component production [S03]; no structural-casting programme identified.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Current OEM-approved imported castings or production beside the platform's established Chinese/other supplier base; strongest facility UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: platform nomination, tooling utilization, structural quality and delivered part cost.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: proximity helps bulky parts only if local platforms actually use and localize that casting family.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: vehicle totals cannot be converted into casting demand without part count, model mix and localisation scope.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: alloy cleanliness, vacuum/heat-treatment needs, tooling/IP, inspection, grid capacity and scrap management.
captured_status: UNKNOWN: wheel MoU [S04] is a different process and cannot prove structural-casting capture.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: contract-backed utilization and avoided bulky-part logistics offset tooling and process qualification.
cheapest_kill_test: Does any reachable assembler have an unawarded structural-casting family suitable for this process?
decisive_evidence: FACT: component localization is an active government agenda [S03]. S04 covers wheels, not structural die-castings.
key_unknown: Actual part/process demand and whether model volumes support dedicated tooling.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 45-min desk/RFQ brief: identify one Allur/Kia platform's casting drawings/BOM and sourcing plan; ask process vendor for required line scale and indicative conversion cost.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Named buyer confirms an open part family, process qualification and pooled model volumes above vendor breakeven at import-competitive cost.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if target platforms do not need the proposed castings/process; PARK if nominations/volume cannot amortize tooling under realistic contract duration.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT for a precise part-level test. Neither assembly growth nor a wheel agreement proves or disproves structural-casting demand.

opportunity_name: Aluminium extrusion for transport and mounting
investor_capital_decision: Industrial extruder installs press and finishing for wagon/bus and proposed mounting profiles at the proposed Kostanay location.
buyer_market: Transport OEMs and mounting-system purchasers; qualified profile mix and tonnes UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: Stadler announced aluminium carbody workshops in Astana [S06]; open extrusion procurement is not established.
strongest_realistic_alternative: OEM-qualified imported profiles and existing regional extruders; strongest large-profile supplier UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: profile envelope/alloy qualification, order density and delivered price, not national aluminium output.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: shorter replenishment might help, but Kostanay is neither the disclosed carbody site nor a proven molten/billet integration.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: train/vehicle numbers do not establish tonnes of press-compatible profiles or a viable press load.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: press size, long-profile logistics, heat treatment, finishing and suitable billet supply.
captured_status: FACT: downstream carbody expansion is announced [S06]; no evidence its profile contracts are unawarded.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: lower freight/inventory and short-run service, conditional on qualified volumes and billet terms.
cheapest_kill_test: Is there an open transport-profile requirement that existing qualified suppliers cannot serve as competitively?
decisive_evidence: FACT: Stadler's issuer release describes welding/painting investment [S06]; it does not announce an extrusion plant or supplier tender.
key_unknown: Whether open transport/mounting tonnes can share a commercially viable extrusion line.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 45-min desk/RFQ brief: obtain Stadler Kazakhstan's profile schedule and sourcing status; match alloy/section envelope to a vendor's press throughput, billet quote and current approved-supplier price.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Open qualified profile orders cover quoted breakeven press load, with delivered cost/service advantage versus the current approved supplier.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if required sections cannot be made on the proposed line; PARK if qualified incumbent supply wins after tooling, finishing and billet freight.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. A real downstream investment warrants a targeted procurement test; it does not validate a Kostanay extrusion build.

investor_capital_decision: Grinding-media producer builds a regional plant using suitable Kazakh steel, at proposed Pavlodar/Karaganda sites.
buyer_market: Uncommitted Kazakh/Uzbek/Kyrgyz concentrator grinding-ball contracts, excluding already awarded volumes.
why_now: FACT: a signed 15-year KAZ Minerals/ME Elecmetal offtake supports a planned Taldykorgan plant [S07].
strongest_realistic_alternative: Contracted ME Elecmetal/Longteng supply and Chinese imports; Uzbek-side production for Uzbek mines remains a candidate.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: cost per tonne of ore at qualified wear/recovery performance, including freight and steel cost.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local freight savings are plausible, but not unique after the disclosed competing plant and its anchor contract.
scale_view: FACT: planned rival capacity 150 kt/y versus KAZ Minerals consumption up to 70 kt/y [S07]. Residual regional demand is UNKNOWN.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: suitable alloy-bar allocation, rolling/forging and heat-treatment capability, firm power and buyer trials.
captured_status: FACT: anchor offtake and partner choice signed [S07]; commissioning/current build status and residual sales allocation not established.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: recurring consumable margin and freight savings if wear performance holds.
cheapest_kill_test: Is independently contractable demand left after the 15-year anchor award and planned competing capacity?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S07 specifies offtake, 150 kt/y plant and intended 2028 start; this is stronger than historical investor interest, weaker than verified operation.
key_unknown: Can another plant win enough qualified residual demand without relying on KAZ Minerals' awarded volume?
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 60-min desk/RFQ brief: reconcile procurement and contract expiry at two non-anchor concentrators with committed supplier capacity; compare delivered cost per ore tonne after wear trials.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Named residual tenders cover vendor breakeven production and trial-adjusted local supply matches/bests existing supply.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if residual demand fits spare/committed incumbent capacity; FAIL only if the defined target volume is bindingly unavailable or performance-adjusted cost is structurally worse.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. A major opening is already awarded, but that does not prove all regional demand captured. A residual-demand test is cheaper than designing a second plant.

investor_capital_decision: Qualified wear-parts investor builds liner casting/finishing capacity in proposed Pavlodar/Karaganda locations.
buyer_market: Regional concentrator replacement-liner programmes with accessible design rights; uncontracted tonnes UNKNOWN.
why_now: INFERENCE: installed milling creates recurring replacement need; a specific newly open liner programme is not established.
strongest_realistic_alternative: OEM/performance-linked imported metal or hybrid liners; ME Elecmetal lists a 45 kt/y China liner plant [S08].
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: mill availability and lifetime cost per processed tonne, including design and maintenance support.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: proximity can cut stock and shutdown exposure; cheaper steel alone cannot beat inferior liner life or mill throughput.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: installed mill size, replacement cycles, liner technology and winnable tonnes must be separated from grinding balls.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: alloy/heat-treatment control, casting yield, large machining, design/IP, power and qualification.
captured_status: FACT: S07 is a ball contract, not evidence of liner capture. Global qualified liner capacity exists [S08].
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: replacement sales and service premium for proven wear life and faster replenishment.
cheapest_kill_test: Can a target mill qualify local liners and offer a contestable replacement programme?
decisive_evidence: FACT: ME Elecmetal lists separate grinding-media and liner operations [S08]; ball-project evidence cannot validate liner feed, orders or process.
key_unknown: Whether local service/logistics savings survive OEM qualification and life-cycle performance.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 45-min desk/RFQ brief: obtain Aktogay's mill model, last liner order/contract expiry and trial criteria; price one replacement set from local-process vendor versus approved OEM supply.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Open trial/contract and repeat demand support quoted foundry scale; warranted liner life/throughput offsets delivered conversion cost.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if proprietary qualification/design excludes the proposed supplier; PARK if incumbent lifetime cost and lead time erase the local margin.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. This is a distinct recurring product decision; neither steel output nor the ball-plant award answers its qualification/economics test.

investor_capital_decision: Rail-component foundry builds qualified side-frame, bolster and coupler casting/finishing capacity in Kazakhstan.
buyer_market: Kazakh and eligible regional 1520-mm wagon builders/repair depots; addressable non-Russian volume UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: rail supplier investments and foundry modernization were reported [S09]; present product-specific gap is not established.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing domestic foundry capacity plus qualified Chinese/Russian imports; strongest eligible supplier depends on part and destination.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: rail-part certification, fatigue/quality reliability, tooling utilization and delivered cost.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local fleet proximity helps, but incumbent modernization may have the same advantage.
scale_view: FACT: 2,565 wagons built in 2024 [S09]. Fleet stock is not annual casting demand; repair/export needs not sized.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: steel casting/heat-treatment capability, destructive testing, certification, power and recoverable yield.
captured_status: FACT: Railcast's current presentation lists forgings/axles [S10]; this cannot prove all target steel castings captured. Vostok scope/current utilization unresolved.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: qualified replacement/newbuild sales with freight and inventory savings.
cheapest_kill_test: Are these exact casting families already supplied locally at sufficient qualified capacity?
decisive_evidence: FACT: GTAI records foundry modernization [S09]; Railcast's disclosed forged-product list differs from the proposed casting package [S10].
key_unknown: Part-by-part incumbent certificates, installed output and uncontracted regional repair demand.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 60-min desk check: map side frames, bolsters and couplers separately against domestic certificates/output and two buyers' sourcing; compare remaining annual tonnes with foundry breakeven.
pass_condition_if_uwt: A material open qualified part family remains, with reachable regional orders covering economical foundry load and import-competitive cost.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if existing capacity covers reachable needs; FAIL only on demonstrated absence of eligible demand or an unachievable mandatory certification.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. Product-specific capture must be checked; a forging plant and a generic foundry announcement are insufficient grounds for FAIL.

opportunity_name: Woven PP sacks and FIBC bulk bags
investor_capital_decision: Woven-packaging investor builds extrusion, weaving and bag/FIBC conversion near proposed southern milling customers.
buyer_market: Bulk agricultural, fertilizer, chemical and cement shippers; unmet qualified bag demand UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: existing FIBC converter already uses domestic PP and is expanding [S11]; new resin access is not exclusive.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Incumbent Kazakh converters expanding with KPI, then Uzbek/other imported packaging; actual cheapest contract quote UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: total bag cost/strength, labour productivity, freight and stable customer load.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: customer proximity and domestic resin are available to incumbents, so they do not yet differentiate a new plant.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: bag demand must be sized by pack format/reuse, not grain export tonnes alone.
physical_constraint_view: FACT: KPI reports multiple PP grades [S12]. UNKNOWN: allocation, FIBC qualification, labour productivity and site power.
captured_status: FACT: incumbent bag expansion reported in October 2026 [S11]; entire market saturation not established.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: conversion margin and avoided bulky-bag transport, subject to productivity and contracts.
cheapest_kill_test: Does an uncovered qualified customer programme remain after incumbent conversion expansion?
decisive_evidence: FACT: KPI reports existing FIBC bag expansion and domestic PP use [S11]. National resin availability does not create exclusive input rent.
key_unknown: A differentiated format/contract or delivered-cost gap large enough for another strategic plant.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK. Undifferentiated conversion competes with expanding local firms already using the proposed advantage; no fatal market-size or capture conclusion is claimed.

opportunity_name: Hygiene-grade PP spunbond and SMS nonwovens
investor_capital_decision: Hygiene-material producer builds spunbond/SMS roll-goods line at proposed Ontustik/TURAN site using KPI PP.
buyer_market: Regional diaper/hygiene converters; Capable Group is a documented domestic manufacturer [S14]. Contractable roll tonnage UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: Marvik's local spunbond plant opened in December 2025 [S13]; specific hygiene-grade SMS opening remains unverified.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Current qualified Chinese/Turkish/Russian roll supply and existing domestic spunbond; exact best hygiene-grade supplier UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: approved softness/barrier/basis-weight consistency at delivered price and line utilization.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: domestic resin and shorter lead time could help; generic spunbond output cannot substitute for converter-approved hygiene/SMS.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: finished diaper consumption is not roll-goods demand without actual converter output and bill of materials.
physical_constraint_view: FACT: KPI reports multiple PP grades [S12]. UNKNOWN: required spinning grade/additives, SMS equipment and converter trials.
captured_status: FACT: Marvik supplies medical/agricultural/construction uses [S13]; hygiene qualification and spare SMS capacity not established.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: roll conversion margin and lower replenishment/inventory costs for nearby converters.
cheapest_kill_test: Do named converters need enough uncommitted hygiene-grade rolls that current domestic/general spunbond cannot supply?
decisive_evidence: FACT: local spunbond and a real diaper converter exist [S13,S14]; neither source establishes an approved hygiene/SMS supply contract.
key_unknown: Qualified hygiene-grade demand versus line scale and incumbent landed price.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 45-min desk/RFQ brief: collect Capable plus one regional converter's roll specifications, annual consumption and approved-supplier quotes; check Marvik grade coverage and line-vendor breakeven.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Buyer-approved open roll volume covers vendor breakeven utilization, with suitable PP allocation and delivered cost competitive against approved imports.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if target product cannot satisfy mandatory converter specifications; PARK if regional open roll tonnage is below efficient scale or existing approved supply dominates.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. A plausible resin/customer mechanism remains, but generic nonwoven capacity must not be confused with hygiene-grade product or reachable demand.

investor_capital_decision: Geosynthetics investor builds membrane extrusion in proposed Atyrau/mining-region location, conditional on suitable domestic PE.
buyer_market: Mine/tailings/leach and water-project contractors in Kazakhstan and nearby eligible markets.
why_now: FACT: domestic PE target remains 2029 [S17]; operator QazGeoMax reports technical commissioning and a 2026 industrial regime [S15].
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing Kazakh membrane converters using imported resin, plus qualified Chinese/regional membrane supply.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: accepted membrane specification, delivered installed cost and reliable project timing.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: proximity is already monetized by local converters; future domestic resin would also be available to incumbents on unverified terms.
scale_view: FACT: QazGeoMax advertises 12m square metres/y at 1 mm [S15]; actual spare capacity and addressable mine specifications UNKNOWN.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: membrane-grade PE allocation, stress-crack/oxidation performance, welding/installation qualification and site power.
captured_status: FACT: local plant is advertised [S15]; this is partial competitive capture, not proof all mine demand is served.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: conversion/installation margin and saved bulky-roll logistics if a differentiated qualified need exists.
cheapest_kill_test: Has the assumed domestic-resin/near-mine advantage already been replicated before the new PE plant starts?
decisive_evidence: FACT: 2029 PE target [S17] and a domestic membrane operation using SIBUR resin [S15] contradict an exclusive first-converter opening.
key_unknown: Unserved specialized mine orders and a contractual resin/cost advantage over existing converters.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK. The defining domestic-resin trigger is distant and the basic local-delivery model already exists. Specialized remaining demand is possible, so no FAIL.

opportunity_name: PE pipe for mining and water infrastructure
investor_capital_decision: Technical-pipe investor builds large-diameter PE extrusion at proposed Atyrau/near-user site using suitable future domestic resin.
buyer_market: Mining, water and irrigation project contractors; buyer/diameter-specific uncovered tenders UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: PE construction targets 2029 [S17]; existing Arystan pipe production is documented [S16].
strongest_realistic_alternative: Established domestic pipe makers and their expansions, then qualified Uzbek/Chinese/Turkish imported pipe.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: diameter/pressure qualification, delivered installed cost, resin grade and continuous project load.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: shorter bulky-pipe freight benefits incumbents too; Atyrau resin origin alone does not beat a converter near the project.
scale_view: FACT: Astana Invest lists 11.5 kt/y polymer pipe/fittings capacity [S16]; exact large-diameter mining coverage UNKNOWN.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: PE100 grade allocation, pressure certification, extrusion diameter range, grid/water and installation capability.
captured_status: FACT: domestic pipe operation exists [S16]; no claim it covers every mining specification.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: extrusion margin and avoided freight of hollow pipe, conditional on tenders and utilization.
cheapest_kill_test: Does future local resin create a new cost advantage versus existing qualified domestic extrusion?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S16 documents domestic pipe capacity; S17 still puts the new domestic resin supply in 2029.
key_unknown: A distinct unserved diameter/specification and firm resin netback that incumbents cannot match.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK. The input trigger is distant and the location mechanism already belongs to domestic converters; an undifferentiated new line is weak promotion material.

opportunity_name: Atyrau PTA and PET bottle resin
investor_capital_decision: Polyester/resin strategic investor funds PTA/PET bottle-resin capacity linked to Atyrau PX; sponsor configuration still requires confirmation.
buyer_market: Central Asian bottlers/resin converters; export tonnes and qualified customer commitments UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: KMG's 2025 reporting still describes an unselected strategic partner and unsettled financing/configuration [S19].
strongest_realistic_alternative: Qualified imported PET from China/Turkey and rival integration near consuming bottlers; strongest delivered supplier UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: PX/other feed netback, conversion scale, freight and qualified export utilization.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: FACT: historical design links Atyrau refinery PX to PET [S18]. INFERENCE: feed integration may help, but does not establish a cost advantage.
scale_view: FACT: historical 735 kt/y PET design [S18]. Regional demand balance and required export share UNKNOWN; nameplate is not reachable sales.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: PX allocation/output, MEG and other feeds, utilities/water, logistics and bottle-grade qualification.
captured_status: FACT: strategic partner not selected in latest retrieved sponsor reporting [S19]; no current binding entry right or FID established.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: integrated feed/conversion margin and lower regional resin freight if utilization is export-competitive.
cheapest_kill_test: Is there a live partner-accessible project with enough reachable sales to run the proposed integrated scale?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S18 identifies Atyrau/PX and design; S19 leaves partner/configuration open. The later report does not reconfirm the earlier nameplate/site detail.
key_unknown: Live project configuration and whether regional/import-parity economics support commercial-scale utilization.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 60-min desk/RFQ brief: reconfirm sponsor partner slot/site/scale and PX/MEG terms; construct a regional PET import-demand bridge and compare landed supplier quotes at quoted breakeven load.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Sponsor confirms accessible equity/operating role; eligible buyers can absorb breakeven output and conservative integrated delivered cost matches qualified imports.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if sponsor confirms no accessible capital role for the defined project; PARK if necessary exports lack a credible price/logistics route or cheap imports defeat the margin.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. A disclosed partner search is real capital-decision evidence, but the decisive market/utilization and comparative cost questions remain open.

investor_capital_decision: Polyester investor builds staple-fibre conversion linked to proposed Atyrau PTA; captive/shared/purchased PTA scope UNKNOWN.
buyer_market: Prospective Uzbek/Turkish spinners; fibre mix and unawarded orders UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: sponsor's PTA/PET configuration remains prospective [S19]; this is not evidence of a committed fibre-grade feed chain.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Established fibre producers near spinners in China/Turkey and importing qualified fibre; strongest plant-specific supplier UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: qualified fibre delivered cost and high utilization, including PTA/MEG, energy and outbound freight.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local PX is several process steps before fibre; any feed gain must exceed new-chain capex and distance to spinners.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: no qualified fibre tonnes or independently executable PTA procurement established.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: actual PTA/MEG access, polymer/fibre quality, spinning line, water/energy and outbound logistics.
captured_status: UNKNOWN: no evidenced open fibre project. S18/S19 concern PTA/PET and cannot be treated as fibre investment rights.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: feed integration plus fibre conversion margin; conditional and not demonstrated.
cheapest_kill_test: Can this fibre plant obtain competitive qualified PTA without assuming another uncommitted upstream project?
decisive_evidence: FACT: KMG still treats PTA/PET as prospective with partner/configuration unresolved [S19]; historical bottle-resin design [S18] is not fibre feed allocation.
key_unknown: A bankable fibre-grade feed chain and nearby-spinners delivered-cost advantage.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK. Multiple upstream dependencies and conversion/export steps dilute the stated location advantage; no immediate buyer/partner trigger justifies work for this deadline.

investor_capital_decision: Licensed explosives/services investor builds emulsion matrix capacity and mobile manufacturing fleet for mine contracts; no separate detonator plant assumed.
buyer_market: Kazakh/regional open-pit mines paying for explosive/blast performance; contestable contracts UNKNOWN.
why_now: INFERENCE: mine operations/expansions create repeat demand; future AN capacity alone does not create an open blasting contract.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing licensed local full-service blasting providers, including INTERRIN [S20], versus a new entrant at the same mine.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: safe permitted on-mine service and cost per acceptable blasted volume, not AN tonnage alone.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: FACT: incumbent already has own emulsions, charging fleet and depots [S20]. INFERENCE: new entrant needs a specific uncovered contract/performance gap.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: contestable blasted volumes, contract duration and minimum matrix/MMU fleet load.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: current suitable AN contract, explosives/security permits, depot access, qualified personnel and mine approvals.
captured_status: FACT: integrated service model already operates [S20]; all regional mine contracts are not proven closed.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: recurring contracted service margin and reduced explosive transport/handling costs.
cheapest_kill_test: Is there a named mine procurement programme open to a newly licensed matrix/MMU supplier?
decisive_evidence: FACT: INTERRIN discloses integrated drilling/blasting, own emulsions and charging equipment [S20]. This refutes a generic service vacuum, not every remaining opening.
key_unknown: Accessible multi-year mine volume and a quantified performance/service gap against incumbents.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 45-min desk/RFQ brief: check Aktogay or SSGPO blasting contract expiry/tenders and performance KPIs; obtain permit checklist, suitable AN offer and matrix/MMU vendor cost before any plant design.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Open eligible contract covers economic fleet/matrix load; compliant feed and permits are obtainable and blast-cost/performance offer beats the incumbent.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if mandatory permit/customer-access requirements cannot be met; PARK if contracts are closed or incumbent service leaves no economic performance gap.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. An additional specialist can earn on a specific mine contract; national mining scale and a future fertilizer project are insufficient proof.

investor_capital_decision: Strategic cyanide investor buys equity and funds extra capacity/safety qualification at existing Talas Karatau operation.
buyer_market: Regional gold-leaching mines; additional qualified contracted demand UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: DBK marks second-stage project financed [S21]; ICMI still lists Talas as not yet certified [S22].
strongest_realistic_alternative: Financed incumbent expansion under existing ownership, plus qualified imported cyanide.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: genuinely available ownership role, delivered compliant supply cost and utilization.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: brownfield integration can help, but existing financing removes a demonstrated need for new expansion equity.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: current commissioned capacity/output and incremental contracted demand; historic expansion plans are not present demand.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: current feed/energy terms, safe transport and buyer qualification. FACT: ICMI designation is not certification [S22].
captured_status: FACT: second-stage funding structure recorded [S21]; operation/commissioning and any offered equity stake remain unverified.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: brownfield margin, safer regional delivery and incremental output, conditional on an actual purchasable stake.
cheapest_kill_test: Does the stated second-line funding/technology opportunity still exist after recorded financing?
decisive_evidence: FACT: DBK financed status [S21]; current certification register says designated, not yet certified [S22]. Neither establishes a strategic stake for sale.
key_unknown: Whether owners offer any equity/expansion role that changes an already financed capital decision.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK. The stated financing opening is already advanced under existing sponsors and the residual entry mechanism is weak. Financing does not legally preclude a later share sale, so no FAIL.

opportunity_name: Container glass linked to Zhambyl soda ash
investor_capital_decision: Container-glass strategic investor builds bottle/jar furnace in proposed Zhambyl/TURAN area using suitable soda, sand and gas.
buyer_market: Regional beverage/food bottlers with compatible bottle/jar orders; open tonnes UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: contractor reports funded Qazaq Soda construction in 2026 [S23]; actual soda commissioning/sales terms are not confirmed.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing domestic container-glass furnaces and qualified Uzbek/imported bottles; brownfield furnace expansion may dominate greenfield.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: gas/batch/cullet costs, freight to bottlers, product mix and continuous furnace utilization.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: soda proximity may save one input leg but can be outweighed by fuel and transporting empty bottles to customers.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: uncontracted bottle tonnes after incumbent supply; beverage growth alone does not size an economical furnace.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: continuous gas allocation, suitable low-contaminant sand, cullet collection, water and bottle quality.
captured_status: FACT: EuroCrystall already makes containers [S24]; float-glass capacity cannot be counted as container supply. Remaining opening UNKNOWN.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: conversion margin and avoided empty-container freight, conditional on fuel/input terms and high utilization.
cheapest_kill_test: Do uncovered nearby bottler orders justify a furnace after existing container capacity and brownfield options?
decisive_evidence: FACT: soda project has contractor-confirmed construction/funding [S23]; existing bottle/jar production is documented [S24]. No new bottle offtake is shown.
key_unknown: Whether a Zhambyl-site batch/fuel advantage exceeds incumbent expansion and distance-to-bottler costs.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 60-min desk/RFQ brief: collect two bottlers' annual bottle mix, supplier prices and contract availability; obtain gas/sand/cullet/soda offers and compare one furnace-sized mix with incumbent expansion.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Compatible open orders cover vendor breakeven furnace load, with firm gas/material availability and delivered bottle cost at least matching qualified alternatives.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if firm continuous fuel/required batch quality is infeasible; PARK if reachable orders or landed margin cannot support an economical furnace.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. Heavy-product freight is a plausible mechanism and soda construction is real; neither proves the right furnace location or enough uncovered bottle demand.

opportunity_name: Solar cover glass linked to Zhambyl soda ash
investor_capital_decision: Solar-glass investor builds rolled/cover-glass line near proposed Zhambyl/TURAN soda supply.
buyer_market: Module manufacturers, not solar EPCs buying finished modules; reachable qualified glass tonnes UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: soda construction is real [S23]; solar-glass producer reports industry overcapacity [S25]. Solar deployment is not glass procurement.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Established Chinese/Asian solar-glass supply near module factories; proposed Kyzylorda solar-glass capacity is an additional future competitor [S26].
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: low-iron silica/optical quality, fuel cost, module qualification and sustained throughput at delivered price.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: soda access alone is weak differentiation against qualified scale producers; distance from module customers may erase freight protection.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: regional module production/orders are not established. A proposed 500 t/day rival [S26] is a plan, not actual local demand.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: low-iron sand, continuous gas, rolling/coating technology, yields and customer qualification.
captured_status: FACT: Kyzylorda solar-glass line is announced [S26], not proven financed/operating. No distinct Zhambyl customer contract established.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: qualified glass conversion margin and freight savings only where module factories actually buy locally.
cheapest_kill_test: Does reachable module manufacturing absorb efficient solar-glass output at prices covering competitive conversion cost?
decisive_evidence: FACT: Xinyi discusses overcapacity in 2025 results [S25]; local solar-glass plan exists [S26]. Neither supports a protected Zhambyl sales pool.
key_unknown: Module-maker orders and a qualified delivered-cost advantage robust to incumbent spare capacity.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK. The proposed feed linkage does not address the dominant customer/qualification/overcapacity issue; a large furnace is weak promotion material under this deadline.

investor_capital_decision: Oilseed processor builds combined crush/clean/dehull operation near Kostanay/North Kazakhstan seed supply.
buyer_market: Prospective EU industrial/food buyers and Chinese/local meal/feed buyers; distinct oil/meal/cleaned-seed offtake UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: EU increased Russian/Belarusian agricultural duties [S27]. Exact current linseed product/origin rates require verification.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Exporting Kazakh seed to destination crushers in Belgium/China and existing Kazakh multi-seed crushers [S28].
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: whole-seed versus local oil/meal/cleaning netback after quality, tariffs and two-product logistics.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: origin diversification can benefit raw seed too; it does not automatically reward locating crushing in Kazakhstan.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: uncommitted seed and qualified product orders, excluding seed already competitively bought by exporters/incumbents.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: seed contracting/quality, oil extraction yield, food-safety capability, storage and separate oil/meal freight.
captured_status: FACT: Maslo-Del already processes flax and exports co-products [S28]; new distinct product/customer slot UNKNOWN.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: crush and cleaning margin plus coproduct sales exceeding raw-seed export netback.
cheapest_kill_test: Does processing locally earn more than selling the same seed to existing crushers after all product logistics?
decisive_evidence: FACT: EU policy change exists [S27], and domestic flax processing exists [S28]. Neither proves an incremental local-processing premium.
key_unknown: Positive local-processing netback across seed price/yield/freight ranges, with legally verified origin/product treatment.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 60-min desk/RFQ brief: compare one EU buyer's raw-seed offer with oil/meal/cleaned-seed bids, yield and freight; verify current CN/origin tariffs and meal outlet.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Traceable Kazakh seed and qualified orders support economic scale; local product netback exceeds raw-seed sale after conversion and logistics across a defensible downside range.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if raw-seed sale or incumbent crushing wins at realistic bids; FAIL only on an evidenced mandatory market-access barrier or structurally negative conversion contribution.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. A real origin-policy trigger deserves testing, but raw-export advantage must not be mistaken for a Kazakhstan crushing advantage.

opportunity_name: Pulse-protein fractionation with later wet-isolate phase
investor_capital_decision: Ingredient processor builds dry pulse milling/air classification; later wet-isolate phase stays conditional within the recorded business.
buyer_market: Qualified food/pet-food/feed ingredient buyers in EU/China/Turkey; concentrate and isolate orders must be tested separately.
why_now: INFERENCE: source proposes rising pulse supply/raw exports; a current qualified concentrate shortage is not independently established.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Canadian/Chinese ingredient plants and importing established qualified concentrates; Canada has evidenced pulse/logistics/power location advantages [S29].
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: protein functionality/yield and total protein-plus-starch/fibre netback after freight and processing.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local feed could help dry fractionation, but raw pulse exports do not prove usable feed mix or food-ingredient competitiveness.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: feed-grade mix versus food-grade suitable peas/lentils, contractable ingredient volume and coproduct outlets.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: dry yield/quality and stable feed. Wet phase additionally needs water, effluent capacity, energy and isolate approval.
captured_status: UNKNOWN: no specific open Kazakhstan buyer nomination or partner slot. Existing foreign plants demonstrate competition, not local capture [S29].
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: ingredient premium plus coproduct realization above raw-pulse export value; each phase must pay independently.
cheapest_kill_test: Will buyers accept concentrate from the actual local pulse mix at a price/yield supporting dry-process scale?
decisive_evidence: FACT: Roquette's Canadian location rationale cites peas, logistics, workforce and hydro power [S29]. It is a partial wet-process comparator, not proof of dry-line economics.
key_unknown: Accepted dry concentrate functionality and whole-feed netback; later isolate utility/customer case remains separate.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 60-min desk/specification brief: match actual pea/lentil lots to two buyer specs and vendor dry-separation yields/costs; request coproduct bids. For wet phase obtain separate water/effluent and isolate requirements.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Dry-stage buyer/specification and supplier yield evidence support positive netback at quoted economic load. Wet phase advances only after its own buyers and utility economics pass.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if actual feed cannot produce the required acceptable concentrate; PARK if dry netback loses to raw export. A wet-phase failure cannot be silently hidden or used to invent a different dry business.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. The dry phase offers a bounded functional/economic test; neither a generic protein trend nor later wet isolation is credited as proven upside.

investor_capital_decision: Fermentation strategic investor takes equity and supplies technology in proposed Kostanay wheat deep-processing capacity.
buyer_market: Regional compound-feed makers; specific amino acids, eligible destinations and qualified offtake UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: QIC names existing sponsors and Myande equipment/engineering role under a memorandum [S30]. A vacant fermentation/equity role is not demonstrated.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Delivered Chinese corn-based amino acids and existing project partners; strongest product-specific supply chain UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: open technology/equity access and amino-acid cost per saleable tonne after substrate, yield, energy and coproduct credits.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local wheat/coproducts may help; neither crop price nor generic engineering agreement establishes fermentation competitiveness.
scale_view: FACT: QIC reports 430 kt/y wheat input design [S30]; this is not amino-acid output or regional feed-additive demand.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: strain/IP rights, sterile process capability, wheat-to-sugar recovery, utilities, effluent and product approvals.
captured_status: FACT: sponsor/engineering parties named [S30]; closed fermentation licence/equity exclusivity is not established. No FID inferred from MoU.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: competitively converting wheat sugars into amino acids while selling gluten/feed/other coproducts.
cheapest_kill_test: Has the proposed strategic technology/equity role already been awarded or does no such open role exist?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S30 identifies KazFoodProducts, Baiterek Venture Fund, Myande and regional authorities; it does not prove all technology or equity roles closed.
key_unknown: Actual available role and product-specific fermentation yield/cost versus delivered Chinese supply.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 45-min desk/sponsor brief: obtain latest project cap table and fermentation licensor/work-package allocation; if role remains open, compare one amino acid's wheat/yield/utilities/coproduct cost bridge with current delivered bids.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Sponsor confirms investable role and available competitive technology; named regional demand supports economic load at import-competitive cost.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if the defined technology/equity role is bindingly unavailable; PARK if wheat fermentation loses after realistic yields or obtainable demand is inadequate.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. An engineering partner alone does not kill a fermentation investor role; public evidence also cannot establish one. Check access before modelling.

investor_capital_decision: Malting strategic investor builds northern/eastern malt house with contract-grown malting barley.
buyer_market: Western Chinese and Central Asian breweries buying approved malt; named open demand UNKNOWN.
why_now: INFERENCE: barley logistics pressure is a source hypothesis; converting barley to malt does not itself remove border/approval constraints.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing Soufflet Kazakhstan malt capacity, Russian malt and qualified supply delivered into each brewery; strongest destination-specific quote UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: malting-grade crop consistency, brewery approval, border access and delivered malt cost.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: proximity to barley can reduce input freight, but incumbent domestic malt competes on the same source-location logic.
scale_view: FACT: current reporting identifies an existing 80 kt/y Tekeli malt plant [S31]. Spare capacity and incremental brewery tonnes UNKNOWN.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: malt-quality varieties, water, heat, crop contracting and Chinese product/plant access.
captured_status: FACT: operating incumbent reported [S31]; not proof all regional brewery contracts are unavailable.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: malting margin and possibly more value per constrained shipment, conditional on actual yield and delivered cost.
cheapest_kill_test: Can suitable local barley and the proposed plant qualify for an accessible brewery programme beyond incumbent supply?
decisive_evidence: FACT: a domestic operating malting incumbent is reported [S31]; no current source establishes the proposed Chinese brewery/plant access.
key_unknown: Approved malting quality and unawarded accessible brewery demand at competitive landed price.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 45-min desk/specification brief: match crop lot analysis to one western-Chinese or regional brewer spec, verify plant/product access, and compare open annual demand with Soufflet/import offers and vendor breakeven.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Suitable contract-grown crop, eligible plant/product route and open brewery volume jointly support viable malt-house load and import-competitive delivered cost.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if mandatory crop/product access cannot be met for the defined buyers; PARK if demand is covered by competitive spare incumbent supply or conversion fails delivered-cost parity.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. Existing malting shows feasibility and strengthens the rival; it does not prove room for a new malt house.

investor_capital_decision: Meat processor builds integrated northern feedlot, export-certified slaughter and boning facility for chilled/frozen boxed beef.
buyer_market: Plant-approved Gulf importers/Chinese buyers; destinations and product forms require separate eligibility.
why_now: FACT: ministry documents resumed frozen-beef trade after 2024 restrictions were lifted [S32]. Current plant approval and export rules remain UNKNOWN.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Approved Kazakh export plants and destination-eligible seaborne beef; strongest rival depends on cut, destination and current tariff/quota rules.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: eligible slaughter/cattle supply and delivered carcass/cut economics after feed conversion and cold chain.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: northern grain access helps only if cattle availability, yield, quota access and logistics beat approved competitors.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: dependable slaughter-ready cattle, quota-eligible export tonnes and buyer orders; herd stock is not plant throughput.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: site/zone animal-health status, approved establishment, halal/GACC route, feedlot water, traceability and cold chain.
captured_status: FACT: existing approved supplier shipped beef [S32]; availability of incremental cattle/buyer slots not established.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: feeding/slaughter yield plus branded or export netback after coproducts and cold-chain costs.
cheapest_kill_test: Can the actual northern site/plant legally sell the intended boxed product and secure enough cattle for utilization?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S32 is country/protocol and existing-shipment evidence. S33 describes March 2026 planned quota-rule relaxation, not enacted October eligibility.
key_unknown: Current plant/zone/product approval and export-allocation conditions, then contracted cattle and destination-specific delivered margin.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 60-min desk/regulator brief: select one original target destination/product; check current veterinary register, zone and quota orders; reconcile a cattle-supply programme with approved-buyer bid and comparable delivered beef offer.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Documented plant/product route and dependable eligible cattle support vendor economic throughput; buyer bid covers feed/slaughter/cold-chain costs versus eligible rivals.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if mandatory zone/plant/product access is unavailable on an implementable path; PARK if cattle or export allocation prevents economic utilization.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. Reopening a country channel is real but does not approve a new northern plant, chilled product, export quota or profitable cattle supply.

opportunity_name: Trans-Caspian container and ro-ro shipping JV
investor_capital_decision: Shipping/port strategic investor charters/acquires shallow-draft container and ro-ro vessels for Aktau/Kuryk crossings.
buyer_market: Forwarders, rail operators and corridor shippers paying freight/charter; uncommitted cargo by vessel type UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: existing line traffic rose in 2025 [S35]; AD Ports awarded two shallow-draft container ships [S34].
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing KMTF/AD Ports fleet and contracted newbuilds, ASCO ferries, or chartering their capacity; best route/operator quote UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: contracted two-way load, cycle time and draft-adjusted annual vessel cash contribution.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: Kazakh cargo origination helps only with enforceable cargo/berth rights; a rival ship can load at the same port.
scale_view: FACT: line carried 59.4k TEU in 2025 [S35]. This is historical throughput, not spare cargo for another JV.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: feasible shallow-draft vessel access, actual sailing load, port/canal permissions, berths, weather and operating/insurance terms.
captured_status: FACT: two 780-TEU newbuilds contracted for Q4 2027 delivery [S34]. Ro-ro and residual container demand not proven captured.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: recurring freight or charter revenue exceeding annual vessel, port, fuel and delay costs.
cheapest_kill_test: Is uncovered cargo/charter demand still sufficient after the committed fleet programme?
decisive_evidence: FACT: signed shipbuilding award [S34] is stronger than an MoU; historical container growth [S35] does not establish a second operator's utilization.
key_unknown: Distinct contractable container/ro-ro deficit and annual full-cycle economics after announced additions.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 60-min desk/operator brief: separate container and ro-ro demand, reconcile monthly sailings/load with current and ordered capacity; compare a charter/acquisition offer plus port rights against committed cargo and incumbent service.
pass_condition_if_uwt: A distinct uncovered vessel-type/cargo slot has credible access and contracted load producing positive annual contribution after full-cycle costs and lower-load sensitivity.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if fleet additions/spare incumbent capacity cover accessible demand; FAIL only if mandatory vessel/port access is physically or legally unavailable.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. The disclosed JV/newbuild programme captures a specific package, but cannot by itself kill all residual container or ro-ro investment.

investor_capital_decision: Shipping strategic investor acquires/charters grain bulkers serving Kazakh Caspian grain exports, separately from container/ro-ro.
buyer_market: Grain exporters/traders serving Iran and other legally/operationally eligible routes; annual cargo commitments UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: ministry recorded vessel shortages in 2025 [S36]; September 2026 specialist reporting again describes tight freight [S37].
strongest_realistic_alternative: Incumbent river-sea/other Caspian grain charters or continuing seasonal spot procurement; strongest available vessel quote UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: annual charter-equivalent contribution after empty returns, draft loss, laytime and seasonal idle days.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: grain origination is fixed in Kazakhstan; dedicated vessels could improve reliability, but ownership domicile gives no inherent ship-cost edge.
scale_view: FACT: Ak Bidai handled 316.5 kt in 2025 [S36]. Ship-available/contractable share and seasonal pattern UNKNOWN; 2026 plan is not a contract.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: draft/load curve, port delivery slots, feasible ship entry, navigation season, insurance and route-specific permissions.
captured_status: FACT: reported shortage persists [S37]; no exclusive acquisition/charter slot or long-term trader contract established.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: freight/charter margin and reliable capacity during shortages; peak spot rates cannot underwrite full-year capex alone.
cheapest_kill_test: Does the shortage support positive full-year vessel economics rather than a brief seasonal freight spike?
decisive_evidence: FACT: ministry actual grain throughput and temporary fleet shortage [S36]; later market report quotes rising Aktau-Iran freight [S37].
key_unknown: Obtainable ship cost and dependable annual laden voyages under real seasonal/draft/return-leg conditions.
next_test_if_uwt: Codex, proposed 60-min desk/operator brief: pair one trader's monthly loading programme with actual bulker charter/purchase and port/insurance offers; calculate full-year contribution at draft-adjusted cargo and observed idle/return legs.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Legally usable vessel/port access and cargo commitments support positive annual contribution and capital coverage at non-peak freight, including low-season sensitivity.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: PARK if profit exists only at shortage-peak rates or seasonality/ballast erases it; FAIL if suitable vessel/route permissions are demonstrably unobtainable.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: UWT. Current bottleneck and real throughput justify a bounded annual-economics test, but freight scarcity alone is not a vessel investment case.

investor_capital_decision: Grain/logistics investor builds silo and stuffing capacity at proposed Khorgos/Dostyk/Altynkol/inland hub and contracts China-bound boxes.
buyer_market: Kazakh exporters/Chinese grain-oilseed purchasers paying handling/logistics charges; incremental throughput contracts UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: Zarya advertises the core Khorgos grain-to-container service already [S38]; generic border congestion is not evidence of missing stuffing capacity.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing Zarya/Khorgos service and Chinese-side transloading or incumbent terminal expansion; route-specific cheapest alternative UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: INFERENCE: control of usable backhaul boxes, train/reception slots, product eligibility and delivered logistics cost.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: new silos cannot create empty containers, Chinese acceptance or rail slots; the existing terminal already has origin/border location logic.
scale_view: FACT: Zarya advertises 15 kt storage and over 1 Mt/y throughput [S38]; actual throughput/spare capacity unverified.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: food-grade boxes, liners, customs/phytosanitary route, rail slots, land and actual available terminal capacity.
captured_status: FACT: operator describes grain container service and historical route permission/shipment [S38]; other locations and incremental demand not proven closed.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: handling/storage margin and low-cost backhaul utilization, conditional on box/rail rights and additional throughput.
cheapest_kill_test: Is the binding constraint actually stuffing capacity rather than container allocation or Chinese/rail reception?
decisive_evidence: FACT: an incumbent advertises the same grain-stuffing service [S38]. Its claimed design capacity is not audited proof of current surplus.
key_unknown: Incremental throughput caused by a new terminal, a real existing-capacity shortage and contractable low-cost boxes/slots.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: PARK. Duplicating a documented service without solving the controlling box/reception bottleneck is weak differentiation; not a proven ban or whole-market FAIL.
